summary: This Makefile snippet sets up a quality assurance workflow using Docker containers to run PHP linting and code formatting tools. It defines color codes, configures a phpqa Docker image with the current PHP version, and then creates four Make targets (phan, php-cs-fixer-dry-run, php-cs-fixer-fix, phplint, yamllint) that run various code analysis and formatting commands inside isolated Docker containers while preserving file ownership.

explanations.1: This assigns the ANSI escape code for blue color to a variable, used later for terminal output formatting.
explanations.8: This uses the `or` function to set PHP_VERSION to 8.1 as a default if it wasn't already defined (presumably from a .env file).
explanations.10: This constructs the full Docker image name by inserting the PHP_VERSION variable into the base image name jakzal/phpqa.
explanations.13: These are standard Docker options: -it keeps it interactive, --rm cleans up after, -v mounts local directories so the container can access your project files.
explanations.16: This shell command gets your current user and group IDs and formats them for Docker's -u flag, so files created in the container have the same ownership as your user.
explanations.19: This combines all the Docker setup variables into one reusable command string that will be used by each Make target.
explanations.25: The eval keyword in Make evaluates the result of the shell command and stores it in a local variable called COMMAND, which is then referenced later in the target.
explanations.26: The printf with \e[1;${COLOR_YELLOW}m colors the output yellow; the @ symbol prevents Make from echoing the command itself.
explanations.31: This runs the previously constructed Docker command with the phan tool, using the command string that was stored in the COMMAND variable.
